top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on a new principle, Katori's magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the light shift so many atoms can be interrogated without perturbing the clock transition, followed by Ye's demonstration of 10^-18 with fully measured systematics and many-body effects. The result is reproduced and intercompared across independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE, NPL), and the two-name allocation (originator and perfecter) is the cleanest available. I accept that it is invention and refinement more than surprise, and the citation should stay narrow and say nothing implying that ion clocks are not competitive. P002 is a genuine and verified discovery, but its allocation (Mele, Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal left out, and QSH and QAH bundled) is not defensible with three names, so it ranks second. A prize is better than no award because the scientific record for P001 is already sufficient.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my field (superconducting circuits, WACQT) is not part of either proposal, though P001 and P002 are outside my expertise only in the sense that I defer to colleagues on topological materials
